Exploring the Cultural and Heritage Landscape of Chhattisgarh

01 Nov 2026, 10:27 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.incredibleindia.gov.in

2 min read

Key takeaways

Overview of Chhattisgarh

Chhattisgarh, situated in central India, is promoted as an emerging travel destination characterized by its integration of tribal heritage, ancient architectural monuments, and biodiversity. The region serves as a repository for historical traditions, ranging from 14th-century temple architecture to age-old textile craftsmanship.

Notable Heritage and Landmarks

  • Purani Basti: Features a historical fort dating back to 1460 AD, complemented by the Budha Talaab and Maharajband Talaab.
  • Bhoramdeo Temple: Often cited for its structural parallels to the Sun Temple of Konark and the Khajuraho complex, this site dates between the 7th and 12th centuries.
  • Danteshwari Temple: A site of religious significance with 14th-century South Indian architectural influences.
  • Kanker Palace: Formerly known as Radha Niwas Bagicha, this early 20th-century structure is now categorized as a heritage hotel.

Nature and Wildlife

  • Waterfalls: Highlights include the Chitrakote waterfall, referred to as the "Niagara of India," and the Tirathgarh waterfall, also known as 'The Milky Falls.'
  • Caving: The Kailash and Kutumsar Caves are noted as the world's second-longest natural caves, extending two kilometers and reaching depths of 35 meters.
  • Conservation: The Achanakmar Tiger Reserve, designated under Project Tiger in 2009, covers 557 square kilometers in the Bilaspur district.

Cultural Traditions

Chhattisgarh maintains various traditional art forms, including:

  • Handicrafts: Production includes bell metal works (brass and bronze), bamboo art, and Loha Shilp (raw metal artifacts).
  • Textiles: Traditional weaving and hand printing using natural vegetable dyes, particularly with Kosa thread.
  • Festivals: Events such as the 75-day Bastar Dusshera and the Hareli festival, which celebrates the agricultural harvest.

Practical Information

Travelers interested in visiting these locations can access the state through the Swami Vivekananda International Airport (RPR) in Raipur. The region also hosts the Indira Kala Sangeet Vishwavidyalaya, which is described as India's first university dedicated to music, dance, theatre, and fine arts. For official updates on tourism, heritage sites, and travel guidance, visitors are encouraged to consult the official Incredible India portal.
